ing: or spinach, stems trimmed; use 1.5 lb spinach if no taro leaves
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Wash the taro leaves and trim the thick stems.
Mix the corned beef with the onion in a bowl.
Make a bowl shape with 3 or 4 leaves overlapping on a sheet of foil.
Spoon in a portion of the beef mixture and [[0.33 cup]] coconut milk.
Fold the leaves over to form a closed parcel and wrap in foil.
Repeat to make several parcels and place in a baking dish.
Bake until the leaves are completely soft.
Open carefully, season with salt if needed, and serve with boiled root vegetables.

ing: or spinach; use 1.5 lb spinach if no taro leaves
st: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Wash the leaves and trim the stems.
Mix the lamb with the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Layer leaves overlapping on foil to make a cup.
Fill with lamb and [[0.33 cup]] coconut milk.
Fold the leaves over, then wrap in foil tightly.
Place the parcels in a baking dish.
Bake until the lamb is tender and reaches 145°F (63°C) or more.
Rest for 10 minutes, then unwrap and serve.
Use only very fresh, sushi-grade fish, since it is not cooked with heat. Cut into small cubes.
Put the fish in a bowl and pour over the lime juice.
Stir to coat and cure in the fridge until the fish turns opaque and white.
Drain off most of the lime juice.
Add the onion, cucumber, tomato and chili.
Pour in the coconut milk and add salt.
Mix gently and chill until very cold.
Serve in bowls or coconut shells right away.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the corned beef and stir, breaking it up.
Add the cabbage in batches, stirring until it wilts.
Pour in the coconut milk.
Season with the salt and the pepper.
Cover and simmer on low until the cabbage is soft and the coconut milk has thickened.
Serve with rice or boiled root vegetables.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk to make a thick, sticky dough.
In a wide pot, combine the brown sugar and [[1 cup]] water and bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer until it becomes a light caramel syrup.
Stir in the remaining [[1.5 cups]] coconut milk and the vanilla.
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering syrup.
Cover and simmer gently without lifting the lid until the dumplings are puffy and cooked through.
Serve warm in bowls with plenty of the syrup.
Cut the watermelon into cubes and remove the seeds.
Peel and chop the ripe mango.
Blend the watermelon, mango and sugar until smooth in batches.
Strain through a coarse sieve if you want a smoother drink.
Stir in the coconut milk and grated coconut if using.
Taste and add more sugar if needed.
Chill in the fridge until cold, then serve over ice.
